Safe fixture probe confirms a session symlink outside the project is accepted and both readers include outside bytes; see probe log.

findings.trigger: Open a project whose .agents/sessions/<slug> directory, or known PLAN.md artifact, is a symlink to a readable file/directory outside the project, then run /resume-plan <slug> or /plan-artifact <slug> PLAN.md.
findings.consequence: The declared project boundary is bypassed. Resume can send outside file bytes to the configured model without general active-read sensitive-path policy. Private-file disclosure is a conditional consequence of such a target; the audit used harmless fixture text and did not read credentials.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve and validate physical project/session/artifact paths before reading, reject paths outside intended workspace/session scope, and apply mandatory sensitive-read policy to the actual target. Keep the check coupled to the opened file to address replacement races.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Create a harmless outside file plus session-directory and artifact-file symlinks; prefix read, page read and resume must reject outside targets while ordinary in-project artifacts still work. The existing safe probe currently shows rejection is absent.

findings.title: Prompt-producing slash commands bypass the active bisection admission guard

evidence.detail: Registered command handler returns before ordinary prompt preflight.
Bisection guard is only after registered command dispatch.
sendPromptCommand checks stream/message/chain occupancy but not active bisection.
Mode trailing prompt calls shared helper directly.
Cancelled bisection checks out newest snapshot tree before releasing its lock.
isTurnBisectionRunning=true probe blocks an ordinary prompt and dispatches /mode:default with the same prompt.

findings.trigger: Start /bisect-turn while no agent chain is running, then submit /mode:default <mutating request>, /resume-plan <slug>, /interview <request> or another prompt-producing registered command.
findings.consequence: The CLI admits an agent run while bisection is rewriting the tracked tree. A later snapshot checkout can replace edits from that concurrent run. The probe establishes admission bypass; real destructive concurrent git execution was not performed.
findings.suggestedFix: Put bisection/attachment preflight in the common prompt admission helper or a single lower transaction boundary used by every user, command, picker, action and queue path; preserve bisection stop/list local controls.
findings.acceptanceProbe: With bisection active, table-test every prompt-producing entrypoint and assert no send/queue admission capable of starting a turn; keep /bisect-turn stop/list reachable. After stopping, the same prompt must dispatch normally.

findings.title: Attached TUI validates local providers before invoking its remote backend

evidence.detail: Attach target is recorded before client creation.
Attach mode selects AcpRemoteBackend, leaving inference to live serve.
Provider readiness runs unconditionally for both in-process and attached clients.
No local config/providers returns not-configured failure.
Real hook + ready remote stub + empty local config yields remoteRuns=0 and inline provider-not-configured error.

findings.trigger: Start a configured serve process, then attach from a TUI process that has no local provider config (or whose local routes differ from the server).
findings.consequence: The remote backend never receives the prompt despite being ready; users are told to configure a local provider for server-side execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Make readiness validation backend-owned. Check local provider routing only for in-process execution; expose and consume ACP server/session readiness/allowed models for remote runs.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Use a ready injected ACP backend with empty/unroutable client-local config and assert its run receives the prompt. Keep fail-closed local readiness tests for in-process execution and explicit remote connection/auth errors.

findings.title: Submission drains non-ready file attachments without including or retaining them

evidence.detail: Slash command execution precedes processing attachment check.
Ordinary prompt preflight checks processing status, not failed status.
All pending attachments are drained.
Only ready file attachments enter model context.
Only ready file attachments are preserved for message display.
Initial asynchronous completion updates only current composer attachments, so a drained processing item cannot settle there.
Processing slash-file and ordinary failed-file probes both remove the pending file and send only bare prompt text.

findings.trigger: Select a file and submit a prompt-producing slash command before its async read finishes; or submit an ordinary prompt after a selected file entered error state.
findings.consequence: The model receives no file bytes or failure note and the file disappears from attachment recovery/message display. A late read result cannot restore the removed item. This defeats guaranteed file-menu context at the send boundary.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate all captured attachments at a single admission boundary. Keep processing/failed items in recoverable state until an explicit retry/remove/approved metadata-only disposition; reserve and commit attachment drains only once an accepted send has the intended context.
findings.acceptanceProbe: For ordinary/slash/picker/queued sends, inject processing, ready, failed and metadata-only files. Processing/failed files must remain recoverable with visible status and no silent dispatch; ready/approved metadata captures must carry provenance and matching content exactly once.

findings.title: Client initialization rejection leaves the turn and queue locked

evidence.detail: Send claims chain/queue occupancy before async setup.
getCodebuffClient is awaited outside the run try/finally.
Owner release/safety reset begins only in the later run finally.
Factory can propagate errors; returned promise is not a never-reject contract.
Mounted submit catch appends generic error without releasing send ownership.
Fault-injected client factory rejection preserves chainBusy=true and canQueue=false.

findings.trigger: getCodebuffClient rejects during initialization or lease/backend setup after message preparation.
findings.consequence: UI displays 'Please try again', but retries observe busy occupancy and queue behind a turn that never started. Resetting the conversation or exiting is needed to release this state. A real factory outage was not caused; the failure contract was exercised through its existing seam.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the complete owned send transaction, including client creation and streaming setup, in one owner-aware cleanup boundary; release only this send's chain/queue occupancy and retain rejected prompt/context for retry.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Inject a client factory rejection and assert chain/queue locks are released, visible failure is retained, attachments/draft are recoverable and the next normal submit is admitted; keep late-old-failure/new-owner tests passing.

findings.title: Validation exceptions become silent resolved submissions

evidence.detail: Validation catch logs and returns {success:false, errors:[]}.
Empty failure errors intentionally produce an empty validationErrors array.
The failed submission returns void after release, with no user-visible error.
Queue item is removed before sending.
Queue restoration sees only rejected send promises.
Production-shaped empty validation failure returns with user/mode messages but no visibleFailure.

findings.trigger: Local validation unexpectedly throws; the real validator catch converts it to a false result with an empty error list.
findings.consequence: The user's cleared prompt appears in history and then work stops without a reason or retry state. For queued prompts, this resolves as successful processing, so unstarted work does not enter rejection restoration.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a visible sanitized validation failure with nonempty error content and communicate a rejected/not-accepted send outcome to queue ownership. Distinguish preparation/validation rejection from accepted run completion rather than using Promise<void> fulfillment for both.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Inject a validator exception in the mounted send/queue path. Assert visible failure reason, queue/draft/attachments retained or recoverable, no SDK invocation, correct ownership release and successful explicit retry after validator recovery.

findings.title: The 100-message cap discards durable CLI transcript before paging can reach it

evidence.detail: Preparation truncates complete live ChatMessage[] to next.slice(-100).
Load previous only increases visibleMessageCount; it does not read discarded history.
Completion persists currentMessages after this truncation.
Serialization persists the supplied message array rather than retaining older blocks.
Envelope and chat-messages sidecar are updated from the same serialized retained messages.
Model continuation history is a separate RunState field.
105 seeded CLI messages plus preparation retain 100 and remove old-0; model history was not involved.

findings.trigger: Continue a conversation whose CLI transcript exceeds 100 messages (including mode/system/bash rows), then send another prompt and allow it to persist.
findings.consequence: Older visible CLI output and prior tool/agent presentation are removed from live and later saved CLI transcript; paging/searching that transcript cannot reach them. This is a bounded-retention design gap, not evidence of SDK model-history loss: RunState/model history and compaction archive are separate and unchanged by this line.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate rendering/working-set limits from durable transcript retention. Keep a paged archive or explicitly documented retention policy with export/recovery before trimming; do not grow the renderer's hot working set without a measured bound.
findings.acceptanceProbe: After >150 CLI messages and a save/reload, the oldest retained-by-policy message must be accessible through archive paging/export or the UI must explicitly disclose the retention cutoff. Separately assert SDK RunState continuity to prevent conflating the two stores.

findings.title: Live plan list/active-session commands are absent from the advertised command catalog

evidence.detail: Executable registry defines /plans and alias plan-ls.
Executable registry defines /plan-use and plan-active/use-plan aliases.
Static menu lists resume/update/status/artifact/lessons but its complete array has no plans or plan-use entries.
Suggestions are derived from that menu array plus skills/presets.
Command palette is passed the same array.
Docs call the menu array authoritative for every registered command.
Docs advertise /plans and /plan-use as ordinary local controls.

findings.trigger: Search slash suggestions or command palette for the documented plan listing or active-session selection command.
findings.consequence: Functional local controls are unavailable through their ordinary discovery surface; users must know hidden typed command names. Registry and catalog have drifted.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the missing discoverable plan commands and aliases, then derive executable and menu metadata from one command contract with explicit hidden entries rather than maintaining parallel arrays.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Every intended discoverable executable command, including plans/plan-use, must appear in slash suggestions and palette, resolve each alias and retain its real local dispatch behavior; explicitly exempt insertion-only or intentionally hidden commands.

domainAssessment.security: Physical containment gap F1 is verified with harmless outside-project bytes. Strengths: project file-menu reads use project containment; initial attachments/retries check mandatory sensitive path policy; approvals preserve complete targets and UUID request identity. Runtime policy, token auth, connector authorization, credential storage/redaction and terminal permission enforcement were delegated and are not proven by UI wiring.
domainAssessment.correctness: F2/F3/F4/F6/F7/F8 are concrete current trigger/consumer mismatches. Ordinary in-process chat, registry readiness, mode/picker routing and local diagnostic controls are mounted and production-wired. Headless/server/replay internals remain delegated.
domainAssessment.state-mutation: Symbol run ownership, separate SDK execution occupancy, identity-guarded archive hydration, atomic normal attachment drain, stale attachment retry rejection and deleted-history filtering are valuable existing guards. F2/F4/F5/F7 identify boundaries not covered by those guards; queue restoration only sees actual promise rejection.
domainAssessment.error-handling: Read/load/provider/diagnostic/render error and retry surfaces are substantial. F5 leaks occupancy after client factory rejection; F6 turns validator exceptions into silent success-shaped processing. Selected-session restore null is silent after App reset. Plan list has batch-level rather than per-session failure isolation.
domainAssessment.performance: Inspected bounds are explicit: 64 KiB plan prefix/pages, batches of 12 plan reads and 32/16 history stats/transcript reads, file preview max 1 MiB/read and 100 KiB characters, 100 shallow directory entries, memoized renderer handler refs and visual message paging. F7 shows an unmeasured retention tradeoff implemented as transcript deletion. No latency/memory benchmark, O(n^2) claim or 'best possible' comparison is made.
domainAssessment.dependency-hygiene: cli/package.json declares the external libraries imported by selected CLI paths and pins Bun 1.3.5, React 19.2.0, and matching OpenTUI core/react 0.5.12. Other dependency ranges and root React overrides exist; full lock/advisory/pruned-install audit was not done here. SDK imports resolve to dist per sdk/package.json, so source-only review is not proof of shipped SDK parity. PATH Bun 1.3.14 FFI failure is a documented toolchain mismatch, not a new product finding.
domainAssessment.test-coverage: Picker-selected tests and bounded adjacent native component/ownership/router cases were read. Nine provider-free safe probe assertions executed under Bun 1.3.5 with the supported OpenTUI preload, 9 pass/0 fail; they assert observed failures, not desired acceptance. Legacy use-ask-user-bridge tests copy helper bodies instead of importing/mounting the hook and do not establish request-ID scope/cleanup. Existing entire CLI/CI schedule, real socket attach and live-provider flows were not run.
domainAssessment.api-contract: Parser/backend dispatch is explicit and protocol paths return before renderer. F1 violates physical project-boundary intent; F3 violates remote execution's client-provider independence; F8 separates executable plan handlers from advertised command catalog. /undo and /redo explicitly preserve files; tracked-file restore is separately labelled preview/exact apply. Full restore/backend contract assurance is delegated.

coverageLimits: Picker selected 18 distinct CLI files / 20 sections / 4,849 lines; every selected section was read. Adjacent evidence expands this receipt to 60 inventory files / 76 merged source sections / 13,848 inspected lines. This is selected-range inspection, not full coverage of all 685 CLI inventory files or every line of these files.
Native query_index/read_files/read_subtree audit tools are repository code and unavailable in this session; actual source inspection used shell numbered exact reads and bounded rg discovery.

Large chat.tsx, SDK event handlers, message persistence, provider and snapshot files were sampled at recorded ranges. Permission policy, credential stores, provider runtime, storage/crash recovery and snapshot restore semantics belong to other shards.

Source files and repository configuration were not changed; credentials and private config values were not read. No external models/providers, live ACP sockets or real destructive git bisection were invoked. Artifacts and harmless probe fixtures were written only under the assigned /tmp evidence/findings paths.

The safe probes use the existing legacy React hook-dispatcher/testing seam and injected SDK/provider results. They prove specific local branches, not full rendered-app/network behavior. Existing native UI tests were read, not executed as a complete suite.
CLI transcript trimming is distinguished from model continuation. No model-context loss follows from the 100-ChatMessage cap alone.
No full advisory database/lockfile/install graph or measured performance comparison was performed.

Attach/detach and inference are opt-in backend choices. Module-only reattach ID and unknown passive stream resume are partial capability boundaries, not an allegation that ordinary in-process chat is broken.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Close physical artifact-read containment
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Prefix/page/resume reject session/artifact symlink escapes and mandatory sensitive targets; normal local artifacts remain usable.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Unify prompt admission across CLI entrypoints
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Ordinary input, command arguments, mode input, plan picker, execution action and queue share bisection and attachment-state checks; none silently loses context or admits concurrent bisection mutation.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Make send acceptance/failure an explicit owned transaction
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Client/validation/preparation failure releases its own occupancy, displays a reason, preserves retriable prompt/context and restores unaccepted queue work without disturbing newer owners.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Make attach readiness and session selection backend-owned
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Ready serve receives prompt with empty client-local provider config; backend connection/auth/readiness errors are surfaced; decide explicitly whether reattach survives process restart.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Separate transcript retention from render paging and restore outcome
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Long saved transcript remains browsable under an explicit archive/retention policy; failed selected-session restore has loading/error/retry/cancel without silently presenting a fresh conversation; SDK RunState is independently validated.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Unify discoverable command metadata and behavioral tests
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Documented plan commands are discoverable with aliases; actual ask-user hook mount/identity/abort/cleanup receives behavioral coverage instead of duplicated helper bodies.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Keep capability maturity grounded in backend evidence
recommendedPlanWork.acceptance: Rate game presets as prompt scaffolds until real detected build targets/job receipts and error/cancellation states are proven. Resolve snapshot/ACP/headless semantics with their owning shards before marking those flows usable; implementation-language expansion should follow measured subsystem needs.

verification.interpretation: Passing probes assert observed current defects. They are audit evidence and must not be mistaken for passing desired acceptance tests.
